updates.title: New visual frames reach open tabs.
updates.body: The visual log now checks for newly published frames while the page is open. Existing frames and the current selection stay in place; Latest frame opens the newest entry. The checked snapshot remains available offline. This is a website improvement, with no new research test or solution claim.

updates.title: The extra-format checks found no valid record.
updates.body: Seven frozen cohorts, containing 2,594 saved readings, completed the registered compatibility replay. All 156 address validations and 30 minikey26 checks failed; the other added formats had no shapes. The independent implementation matched full forms and private validation results. This closes the specified gap on existing outputs, with no new selector or broader puzzle exclusion.

updates.title: A format gap in the saved outputs.
updates.body: Several earlier batches used four record-format gates. The fixed supplemental replay covers seven saved cohorts and additional supported formats, including historical 26-character minikeys where needed. Exact input witnesses, controlled code and a public registration precede target checks. It adds no new reading rule.

updates.title: Read the 40 saved orange-mask texts.
updates.body: Two AI contexts read every historical forward orange-mask text: eight from correct physical page pairs and 32 controls, including two empty entries. Neither recognized a concrete second message or puzzle instruction. This is subjective review of existing outputs, with no new cipher run. Historical geometry limits remain; the paper supplies no specific page-overlay rule.

updates.title: The opener gap is checked. No key found.
updates.body: The declared 151-unit source produced three literal readings and six forms. No valid key-format record passed; an independent implementation agreed. Both AI contexts read all three complete outputs without recognizing a second message. This closes the small opener-line coverage correction only. The scans, code, exact registration and review limits are public.

updates.title: Two opener lines were outside the old frame.
updates.body: A new declared editorial-column model has 151 units: the unchanged 142 body rows and seven displays, plus the opener name and byline. Independent proof checked all nine nonbody units and ordering. One fixed first-chunk/odd/even procedure with literal-format gates is being registered before generation; full-output reviews follow. This is a small coverage correction, not a new cipher theory.

updates.title: Two rows checked. A source limit exposed.
updates.body: All 142 rows / 1,258 tokens received a first contrast review. Independent checks verified the exact source atlas and 22 pilot token masks. A separate three-row field model restores readable interiors but leaves 13 glyph/background joins and edge residue unresolved. It does not certify original glyph support. No new gap decode ran; the full sources, memberships, code and limits are public.

updates.title: The detector matches. Spacing stays open.
updates.body: Traced all 142 rows and 1243 lexical regions after public registration. All 142 first-guard outcomes matched the old run; the same 38 rows still fail. Failed-word/boundary records now support source preparation. Later words after failure are explicitly counterfactual. No gaps, bits, decodes or candidate checks were generated. The visual frame links actual source strips and the 3D page view.

updates.title: Locate the failed word before changing the measurement.
updates.body: The diagnostic is fixed before execution: all 142 rows, the original foreground rule and guard order, and every lexical word region. It records boundary and polarity diagnostics without interword gaps, bits or decoding. Later words after a first failure are labelled counterfactual. Target execution waits for the verified public registration commit.

updates.title: 165 feed entries. The recording date is still open.
updates.body: Recovered a historical RSS capture and checked five fields with nine fixed terms. Four matched items supplied generic contexts; OP65 has empty descriptions and only a publication date. Observed audio routes failed and two exact archive indexes were empty. No audio was recovered; these bounded checks do not clear the creator’s recording windows.

updates.title: 38 rows failed measurement. That leaves spacing open.
updates.body: The old spacing run retained no complete-page result. All 15 standalone punctuation tokens lack geometry; mixed foreground and approximate boxes create source risks. Native source strips are now inspectable. A separately registered diagnostic will identify first-failing words without gaps, bits or decodes; the old frozen results remain unchanged.

updates.title: Three readings. No clear second message.
updates.body: The registered first-word, odd-line and even-line outputs matched across two implementations. Two AI reviewers each read all three complete strings and recognized no clear second message or concrete puzzle instruction. No key-format or network check ran. This is subjective nonrecognition in one fixed source model; encoded keys, other interpretations and the puzzle remain open.

updates.title: The line model is frozen. Three direct readings are next.
updates.body: Two AI visual passes checked all 115 physical rows without a proposed lexical or wrap correction. The declared encoding preserves 111 non-title content rows. A separate protocol registers first chunks, odd whole lines and the even-line control before generation; independent full-output review follows. No mirror variant, key-format sweep or network check is included. Exact issue/date remain unverified.

updates.title: Four text pages read. The line model comes next.
updates.body: One AI assistant read printed108–111 and recognized no explicit puzzle-reading instruction. A private115-row draft preserves printed wraps and separate roles; independent proofreading is in progress before any experiment. This is exploratory nonrecognition, with no cipher stream, key check or network request. Issue/date remain unresolved.

updates.title: A retained column, now visible.
updates.body: Bitcoin and the Funky Upheaval had documented image/style-control work but no owning text-decoding record was located in the bounded audit. Eight scans were fully reviewed and copied byte for byte: six article pages, two separately labelled ads. The six pages now have page-board, layer-stack and mirror views. Exact issue/date remain unverified; no new cipher test is claimed.

updates.title: The 26-character lead: zero history in scope.
updates.body: Python and Node agreed on five fixed mainnet constructions. Both providers returned all ten HTTP200 responses with every chain and mempool statistic zero. An independent saved-receipt review matched the addresses, request coverage, statistics and pins. This provides no funding evidence within those constructions at check time. Other constructions and the puzzle remain open.

updates.title: A message could come before a key. We read for one.
updates.body: Two AI reviewers each read all 22 frozen body-only outputs, including line selections, first-word lists, initials and saved reversals. Neither recognized an actionable intermediate instruction. No new selector or crypto check was added. This is exploratory, unblinded nonrecognition; it does not prove that a message is absent.

updates.title: The weak lead gets a bounded history check.
updates.body: The new history adapter fixes one fingerprint, five standard mainnet address constructions and ten read-only requests across two providers. Node and Python must agree before any query. Synthetic controls and separate code review passed; target execution follows public registration.

updates.title: Reproducible, but the source choices are uncertain.
updates.body: The checksum lead occurs only in the global model: rightmost black selections, reversed row sequence, joined words. An exact allowed path reproduces it, but all 24 nominal readings miss it and uncertain membership choices are required. This establishes reproducibility, without evidence of creator intent beyond the weak checksum.

updates.title: The missing length. One weak hit.
updates.body: The registered 26-character replay completed all 42 frozen forms and 24 mirror language graphs: 207 distinct shaped strings, one eight-bit checksum pass. Independent full-set replay and Node crypto agreed. A chance-compatible pass is not a solved key. Source-witness and separately registered history checks are next; no scalar, address or network lookup ran in this experiment.

updates.title: One missing length. The same readings.
updates.body: Historical Casascius software accepted 26-character mini keys. Our earlier gates covered 22 and 30. A separate replay is being registered for the same 42 frozen forms and 24 mirror language graphs, with independent code and synthetic controls. No new reading or geometry is added; target checking follows public registration.

updates.title: The original clue threads are readable.
updates.body: Normal browser access recovered the three original clue conversations. A contemporary reply identifies the El Salvador issue; other readers’ seed and format guesses add no verified decoding rule. This was a bounded review of visible replies and selected subthreads, not a complete account search.

updates.title: Two December recordings, checked.
updates.body: Two AI assistants each read all 412 and 456 saved auto-caption cues. The December 23 closing supplied a planned December 28 follow-up, and an official episode matches its date and theme. No explicit puzzle-linked extraction rule was recognized. Audio, visuals and the full calendar window remain open.

updates.title: The original episode, recovered and checked.
updates.body: The official OP64 page and English auto captions were recovered through normal browser access. Two AI assistants read all 543 cues; neither recognized an explicit puzzle instruction. Reversal and mirror themes lack an article-linked rule. This is caption-only context; the audio and other date windows remain open.

updates.title: The twelve-step model: 93 shaped strings, zero passes.
updates.body: All 72 registered literal-chunk readings completed; all 93 minikey-shaped strings failed, with no other declared format shape. A separate implementation reproduced every token, reading and evaluation. Sixty readings use source-confirmed glyphs; twelve retain gutter-prefix uncertainty. This excludes the exact fixed model, not every twelve-step interpretation or the puzzle. No address queries were needed.

updates.title: The “12-step” phrase gets one fixed test.
updates.body: All 312 Orange Party body rows have been inspected; 68 rows were corrected, including typography, while three softened word prefixes remain flagged. The 2,018-chunk model now has a 72-reading stride protocol and two controlled implementations. Target selection starts only after public registration; model completion and source certainty will be reported separately.

updates.title: The Orange Party lead: zero history in scope.
updates.body: Independent Python and Node agreed on five fixed mainnet address constructions for the replay’s weak checksum lead. Both providers returned all ten successful responses with zero chain and mempool statistics. This gives no funding evidence through those constructions at check time. The checksum remains valid; other wallet constructions and the puzzle remain open.

updates.title: A missed format check. One weak lead.
updates.body: The exact saved Orange Party readings produced 3,709 distinct forms: 15 shaped WIFs all failed, while one of 205 shaped minikeys passed its eight-bit check. A separate implementation reproduced every record and the result. No hex or BIP39 shapes. This is a chance-compatible checksum lead, not a solution; its bounded Bitcoin-history check is next.

updates.title: Closing a checker gap in another column.
updates.body: The Orange Party scans are restored, and 1,940 saved readings have a fixed replay protocol. The old checker covered WIF and hex, but not embedded minikeys or BIP39. Controls and independent code review are complete; target checking starts only after public registration. This is a coverage audit, not a new cipher theory.

updates.title: The pages and the work, in view.
updates.body: An interactive 3D page board, layer stack and mirror comparison now sit beside a dated visual log. The first three frames reuse completed results, with checked numbers, evidence links and SVG exports for future research films. These views add no new decoding result.

updates.title: Five addresses. No history reported.
updates.body: The weak checksum lead was checked through five fixed mainnet address constructions. Python and Node agreed on all five; Blockstream and mempool.space returned 10/10 successful responses with all chain and mempool statistics zero. This covers only those constructions at the recorded check times. The checksum remains valid, while a funded-key interpretation in this scope has no supporting history. Other wallet constructions and the puzzle remain open.

updates.title: One weak checksum hit. History check next.
updates.body: All 24 registered global language checks completed: 382 distinct minikey-shaped strings, one 30-character 8-bit checksum pass, and no other declared format candidate. A weak checksum does not authenticate a prize. The value stays private; a read-only history check under its own preregistered protocol and source-witness review are next. No network query or transaction has run at this checkpoint.

updates.title: Testing the global combinations without guessing a reading.
updates.body: The page-pair envelope is tested; combinations across all four pairs remain open. An exact graph search is being checked on synthetic cases before registration. The modeled 43-million path count is not a claim of completed checks or independent theories.

updates.title: Another column: 12 shaped strings, zero valid records.
updates.body: Issue 26’s reviewed first words produced 1,746 distinct forms. Both WIF-shaped strings and all ten minikey-shaped strings failed checksums; no other declared format candidate. An independent check agreed. This covers the fixed first-word readings only. Blurred full-line endings remain outside scope.

updates.title: Another eligible column. Its first words are under review.
updates.body: The publisher identifies this matching Keiser column as a Q2 2022 release, before his December hidden-keys post. Earlier work tested its design, not faithful first-word readings. The retained scans are now public; line starts are being checked against the pixels. No key result or alternative 20-BTC target is claimed.

updates.title: 222 shaped strings. All failed the checksum.
updates.body: All 17,108 modeled pair-local boundary paths were checked: 102,648 correlated readings, 93,536 distinct forms. All 222 distinct minikey-shaped strings failed. An independent count/checksum audit agreed. This closes the registered pair-local envelope only; global concatenations and other mirror rules remain open.

updates.title: Resolving the mirror-first boundary cases.
updates.body: Source review is checking which ambiguous words can actually change the first or last selected word. A bounded pair-local envelope will be registered before decoding. The previous incomplete result remains open; no new negative or solution is claimed.

updates.title: Literal machine-readable codes
updates.body: All 384 fixed views were scanned for QR, DataMatrix, Aztec and Code128. 0 payload occurrences. All 16 planted barcode-control views passed. No detector-readable payload in this exact view set; damaged or other codes remain possible.

updates.title: Current raster least-bit payload
updates.body: Checked 768 current-raster RGB least-bit serializations, with strict literal-format validation and no arbitrary scalar/hash guesses. No declared literal key. This is a weak file sanity check; printing, scanning or JPEG may erase an earlier payload.

updates.title: Corrected-leaf alignment specificity
updates.body: True-leaf mean overlap was 0.03085; the strongest wrong pair scored 0.03970. Shift rank was 0.03125, but the preregistered screen also required beating every wrong pair and failed. This weakens that exact alignment claim; it is not proof against all mirror methods.

updates.title: Spectral color-isolation OCR
updates.body: All 112 fixed spectral/baseline OCR views completed, yielding 1038 text streams and 1464 distinct forms. No declared literal key. Controls passed; OCR errors and other color transforms remain outside this result.

updates.title: Reused capsule interior differences
updates.body: Five repeated capsule pairs produced 20 fixed residual OCR views plus combined readings (24 extracted text streams). Positive OCR controls passed; no declared literal key. This excludes only the registered detector-readable residual views, not all artwork encodings.

updates.title: Printed-line displacement channel
updates.body: Obtained 98 of 142 row displacement proxies; 44 rows were unavailable or could not be detrended. No page/global decoding had complete coverage. The registered baseline channel remains inconclusive.

updates.title: Fixed interword-gap binary channel
updates.body: Measured 811 ink gaps across 104 of 142 rows. 38 rows failed optical guards; no full page was complete. Zero page/global decodes were retained or evaluated. The separate audit clarifies that the frozen code first constructed then discarded temporary partial-subset decodes. Spacing remains inconclusive.

updates.title: Orange/black two-alphabet channel
updates.body: 46 physical orange/black fragments were serialized at fragment, word and letter resolution: 1296 labeled decodes, 616 distinct forms. No declared literal key. This excludes only the fixed color-state/Bacon/ASCII serializations.

updates.title: Two-sided printed highlight stencil
updates.body: 0 complete readings; all 40 selection scopes contained uncertain boundary words. No complete stencil decoding was justified. The hypothesis remains open.

updates.body: Only 12 of 120 labeled readings were complete; 36 of 40 selection scopes remained ambiguous at mask edges. The complete readings contain no declared literal key. This does not rule out mirror-first word selection.

updates.title: 12 shaped strings. Zero valid minikeys.
updates.body: A gap in the old checker is closed: it could miss a short minikey inside a longer reading. The fixed scan covered 22 existing readings and 42 exact text forms. All 12 distinct strings that fit the alphabet and length failed the checksum. An independent Python check agreed. This rules out only 22/30-character minikeys in those forms; no address lookups were needed.

updates.title: $KEY404 is live. The contract is public.
updates.body: The founder supplied the official Solana contract. Its mint was checked on mainnet; the site now publishes the exact address, a copy action and the Pump.fun link. No fee receipts, recovered BTC or buybacks are claimed. The case player and README are simpler; the research archive also received a privacy correction.

updates.title: The case in 62 seconds.
updates.body: Fable 5.2 Max created an original film from the article’s printed characters, with a procedural score, timed captions and a transcript. The player loads the movie only on request. The source renderer is public. This is a dated explanation of the hunt and funding plan; no research result changed. The project’s home is now keynotfound.com.

updates.title: One investigation. The work stays public.
updates.body: This is one solver’s investigation, with public files and optional help. Leads, corrections and independent tests are welcome. The site and launch kit now use that first-person voice. Funding remains planned; no research result changed.

updates.title: One map, one ledger, and a role for every reader.
updates.body: The entry page is now newsprint with the marker on NOT. Reader, Skeptic, Solver and future Backer roles sit directly under it, each with one action. The research map and the full ledger are one section: pick a branch or every method, filter by status, search, and open a record for its exact ID, scope, limits, evidence and commands. Research notes are listed apart from site notes; every note stays in the history. Funding separates what is planned, what is committed and what is unknown. No research result changed in this update.

updates.title: One mystery. Four ways in.
updates.body: The research map connects every curated method to a readable branch, its evidence and related field notes. Accepted changes on GitHub sync into the map and update log; downloads remain release snapshots. Repository activity is shown separately from research results. Reader, Skeptic, Solver and future Backer roles make the next action explicit. Newsprint and ink replace the olive palette; the lime marker stays.

updates.title: The claim, the next step, and the funding status.
updates.body: The entry page now explains the hidden Bitcoin-key claim and names what remains unverified. Read, review, and propose links show how to help. Funding leads with the unlaunched status; submissions are reviewed before a dated result is published.

updates.title: A clearer log. A simpler place to talk.
updates.body: All dated updates are visible together. The public guest-chat popup replaces the Nostr connection flow; choose a nickname to join. Research findings still belong in the versioned GitHub archive.

updates.title: 256 bits. Still no key.
updates.body: A disclosed rule turns 24 printed numbers into 256 bits. Four mirror forms were checked across 20 addresses, with no transactions. Another ordinary serialization explains the earlier 264-bit count.

updates.title: Rebuilt the actual printed lines.
updates.body: The 142 body lines were reconstructed and independently checked. Earlier transcripts split words and baselines differently, which matters for the George Sand clue.

updates.title: A promising reflection graph was wrong.
updates.body: All 17 apparent overlap confirmations depended on a matcher joining distant words into large boxes. Those results are retained with the correction rather than quietly removed.

updates.title: The investigation gets a public home.
updates.body: Source scans, corrected transcripts, reproducible scripts, and the history of failed tests are being released as one case file. The puzzle remains unsolved.
